chapter_theme: Songs at Thirukkarkudi (திருக்கற்குடி): the poet confesses the sea of union with women whose breasts overpower even ascetics, and the wealth poured out on them, and fears Yama's messengers who will open his account and torture him by its total; he asks for the feet and for Murugan to come on the peacock, and praises him as the god who was himself caught by the hunter girl's eye.

563.reading: The poet describes women's breasts as conquerors that shatter the pot, chase off the elephant, defeat the mountain peak, crush the flocks of birds and swell so proudly that ascetics of the great principle faint, and asks for Murugan's feet so that he may be free of weariness in the sea of union. The praise names the god who, deeply desiring the hunter girl in the forest millet field, was caught at the corner of her kohl-dark eye, who was born in the pond and revived the heavenly world with his matchless vel, the lord of Thirukkarkudi, famed for Tamil and for poetry.
563.nuance: The breasts are described with the verbs of a conqueror (தகர்த்து, துரத்தி, செறுத்து, குமைத்து), each beating one of the stock comparisons: pot, elephant's temple, hill, the chakravaka birds. குருத் தத்துவத்துத் தவர் சோர, even the ascetics fainting, is the measure of their power. In the praise Murugan is the one caught (மைக்கட் கடைப்பட்டு நிற்கைக்கு உரியோனே).

564.reading: The poet confesses that he poured out wealth on mountainous breasts and was caught in their pleasure for many days, and fell into the stupor of deep sleep; he asks that when Yama's messengers seize, bind, kick, drag, trample, open his bundle of accounts and, according to the total, twist, turn, burn, push him into filth and abuse him, he not be left to wander so tormented, but that Murugan, pleased with his Tamil, come in anger on the peacock with the vel's command in hand and stand at his side. The praise asks Murugan to give him the thought fit to praise him in words, the lord of the devotees at Karkudi, the place of attainment.
564.nuance: கணக்குக் கட்டு விரித்துத் தொகைக்குட் பட்ட இலக்கப்படிக்குத் தக்கபடியே, opening the bundle of accounts and punishing 'according to the figure in the total', makes Yama a clerk with a ledger; the torture is measured by the sum. சுழுத்தி is the state of deep sleep, here the soul's stupor. The poet's claim on Murugan is his Tamil (தமிழ்க்குச் சரித்து). Splits in the first lines (கொடத்துக் கத்தை யவத்தைக் கடுக்கை) are uncertain.

links.note: Both measure women's charms by their effect on ascetics: in 108 their laughter makes renouncers weaken (துறவினர் சோர), in 563 their breasts make the ascetics of the great principle faint (தத்துவத்துத் தவர் சோர), the same verb.

Both list the tortures Yama's messengers inflict, binding, dragging, burning. 558 lists them without a reason; 564 gives them one, an account of the poet's deeds opened and totalled, with the torture matched to the sum.
